text: Using the catalogue, the design positions the ESP32 DevKitC V4 so the micro-USB port faces the short end at −X and the antenna points toward +X; it also puts three 5 mm LEDs in the lid. Nothing may collide, and the layout has to be declared.

Support the board on four pads beneath its two end regions, away from the header footprint, every pad no smaller than 10 mm². The walls plus two stops at the antenna end hold it in place, the stops being 0.2 to 1.0 mm away from the board and under its top face. None of the printed box may intrude on the board's keep-out volumes (header pins, tails, component side).

The antenna keep-out must stay empty of walls and lid. Per the part's data it covers the final 6.0 mm of the board and the 8.0 mm past its end, spanning the board's full width and reaching up to 5.0 mm over the top of the module; the cavity must run at least 8.0 mm beyond the antenna end.

It must be possible to push a micro-USB cable all the way into the board, lid on, through one hole in the end wall at −X. The hole gives the plug at least 0.3 mm of room all the way round, but is no more than 1.5 mm larger than the plug on any side, and at least 1.5 mm of wall remains around it.

In the lid, each of three 5 mm LEDs goes into a collar so its dome is level with the outer surface and its flange is caught by a shoulder with a snap lip behind, which keeps the LED from dropping out. The collar holes measure 5.2 to 5.4 mm across, the flange overlaps by at least 0.2 mm each side, the dome is within 0.3 mm of flush, and the snap-lip opening is 5.3 to 5.6 mm with at least two slits. Arrange the LEDs in a line with at least 10.0 mm between them, and keep every LED axis at least 4.5 mm (in plan) from the board's header-pin and antenna keep-outs.

The box gets a pair of ears, and each carries a countersunk slot sized for a 4.2 mm wood screw. The centres of the two slots are 100.0 mm from each other, and the countersink outline of each slot stays at least 3.0 mm away from its ear's edge and from the box. Every slot is a stadium 4.5 mm wide with 4.0 mm between the centres of its ends (so you can adjust), beneath a 90 degree countersink that is 8.4 mm across. Make the ears 3.5 to 5.0 mm thick, with the slot centres symmetric about the centre of the box to within 0.5 mm.
So the box can lie flat on the wall, its back should be a flat face and the ears must be coplanar with it, within 0.3 mm.

Make the lid a separate piece that sits on the base via a sliding lip and is secured by four M3 self-tapping screws that go into tabs outside the cavity. The screw axes lie 3.5 to 5.0 mm outside the wall's outer face, the pilot holes are 2.4 to 2.6 mm across and at least 6.0 mm deep, and the lid's holes are 3.4 mm. The lip should be at least 2.0 mm deep, with 0.15 to 0.35 mm of clearance on each side.

Once closed, the box may be open only at the USB port, the three LED holes, the screw holes for the lid and the two slots in the ears. Wall, floor and lid thickness should fall between 2.0 and 4.0 mm, and every opening needs at least 1.5 mm of surrounding material.
Each part must be one manifold body that prints without supports: the base resting on its back face and the lid on its outer face.
Overall, counting ears and tabs, the shut box must fit within 125 x 50 x 26 mm, with the long direction running along the 54.4 mm side of the board.
What comes back is a base STL and a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the layout declaration, and the agent's own clearance report, whose figures have to agree with an independent measurement.
